value.title: Cache proxy watch: no false outage from one slow status read (F204)
value.summary: Workstream 004 s05 (F204, req-09). The sidecar's `GET /__pij/status` answers at once from cached readiness and refreshes it in the background, single-flight on `check_lock`; it gains an additive `checked_at_ms`. The daemon's watch declares the sidecar down at once only on a refused connection, and otherwise only after 2 consecutive failed reads (timeout or unreadable), reporting slow reads separately in `/health.cache_proxy.slow` and `just doctor`. The spawn gate retries a timed-out read once before launching plain. No new timer, launch or per-seat work. Also covers the 402 twin of F001 (a stale 402 or 2xx from a request sent with a replaced token changes no state; req-02) and F205 (notices give a seat count and where to list them, never the ids). Delivers workstream 004 s05: F204, F205 and the stale-402 fix; req-02 and req-09.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: At 14:56 on 2026-11-18 the daemon's 30 s watch read `/__pij/status` with a 1 s timeout, got no answer, declared the sidecar "not listening" and sent every prime an outage notice naming 43 proxied seats, while the sidecar (pid 61526) was up, ready and error-free. Two causes, both on main (pm-004's trace): the status route awaits `run_check`, which runs two GitHub GETs (15 s timeout each) whenever the readiness cache has expired (10 min after a success, 60 s after a failure, and on every recheck after a refresh or 402); and the daemon turns the first timed-out read into the outage notice, and gates spawns plain on the same single read. This plan fixes both halves in one PR: the status route never waits on upstream, and the daemon tells a refusal (nothing listens) from a slow or unreadable answer, declaring down on the latter only after two in a row.

sections.name: goals
value: A status read never waits on GitHub: it returns the cached readiness at once and starts at most one background check (req-09: no false outage).

Primes hear of a sidecar outage only when it is real: at once on a refused connection, after 2 consecutive failed reads otherwise; never on a single slow read (row 21's no-false-flap rule), and once on recovery (req-09, F192).
Operators see slow reads apart from outages, in `/health.cache_proxy.slow` and `just doctor`.
A seat spawned during one slow read still comes up proxied.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Startup and `POST /__pij/reload` still wait for their check: the reload contract returns the fresh status.
Changing the readiness TTLs (10 min, 60 s), the watch interval (30 s) or the 1 s read bound.
The F002 402 latch and the F001 install rule: unchanged, their regressions stay green.
s04's live matrix window, the prod daemon, port 7471 and the LaunchAgent.

value.claim: Status never waits on upstream (c-status-route, c-readiness). `GET /__pij/status` derives its body from the cached readiness and returns at once. When the cache has aged out (10 min after a success, 60 s after a failure) or a recheck is owed (after a refresh, a new token or a 402), it starts one background readiness check and returns the current cached state; the check takes `check_lock` with `try_lock`, so concurrent reads and a check already in flight (including a reload's) start nothing more. The background check settles the state when it lands. Startup and `POST /__pij/reload` still run their check inline and return the fresh status. The F002 latch (a 402 holds `quota_exhausted` until a 2xx, the reset date or a reload) and the F001 install rule (facts and refreshes land only for the token generation they were read with) still hold.

`checked_at_ms` (c-status-route). The status body gains `checked_at_ms`: epoch milliseconds of the last completed readiness check, null before the first. Additive: `Status` reads it with a serde default, so a newer CLI still reads an older sidecar; the daemon's `ProxyStatus` carries it into `/health.cache_proxy.status`. Blueprint 003 c-status-route names it.

Watch debounce (c-proxy-watch, req-09, rows 7 and 21). A status read now ends as a status, a refusal (connect failed: nothing listens), a timeout (no answer within 1 s) or unreadable (not 2xx, not the body). A refusal is declared `not_listening` at once, with one notice as today. A timeout or unreadable read is a failed read: the watch declares `not_listening` only on the 2nd consecutive failed read (30 s apart on the watch), with one notice saying it did not answer on 2 reads in a row; a single failed read holds the last declared state and sends nothing. A status reading resets the count. So: one timeout gives 0 notices; two in a row give 1; a refusal gives 1 at once; timeout, ready, timeout gives 0. Recovery after a declared outage gives one notice. The first-read rule (pm-004 ruling) applies to the first declared state.

Slow reads shown (c-proxy-watch, c-doctor-row). `/health.cache_proxy` gains `slow: {count, last_at}`: failed reads (timeout or unreadable) since the daemon started and the epoch ms of the last one. `reachable` and `error` still describe the last read; `state` is the declared state. `just doctor`'s `cache seats:` line appends `slow reads: <count>` with the last time when there is one. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents the field.

Gate retry (c-spawn-gate). When the gate's status read times out, it reads once more, still bounded at 1 s, before deciding; a refusal or an unreadable answer is not retried. If it still ends plain, the receipt says why: `proxy not listening` for a refusal, `proxy did not answer within 1 s, twice` for two timeouts.

Stale upstream answers change no state (c-proxy-core, c-readiness; req-02; the 402 twin of F001). Each forwarded request captures the account and token generation it was sent with. An upstream 402 latches `quota_exhausted` only if that account and generation still match the current holder, the same rule as F001's refresh install; a stale 402 is logged with the account it actually came from and changes no state (the `upstream_402` counter still counts it). A 2xx clears a latched 402 under the same rule, so a request that left with the old account's token can't clear the new account's latch either. Regression: switch to an exhausted account (fake 402), start a request, switch back to a usable account, let the stale 402 return: status stays ready for the usable account and its quota is never latched.

Cost (AGENTS.md; blueprint k-3, k-4, k-5). No new timer, launch or per-seat work. The sidecar's background check replaces the inline one, at the same TTLs: still at most 2 GitHub GETs per 10 min per account while healthy. The watch stays 1 loopback GET per 30 s, constant. The gate adds at most 1 loopback GET per Copilot spawn, only after a timeout. `pij-rs --json ping | jq .data.spawns` on the private daemon, twice a known time apart, shows no new op; spawn_sites.rs unchanged and passing.

Proof and docs. Live on a private daemon and a sidecar on a test port with a fake upstream that stalls: a forced slow readiness check gives no notice and the next Copilot spawn is proxied; a killed sidecar still gives one notice at once. Blueprint 003 c-status-route, c-readiness, c-proxy-watch (and c-spawn-gate for the retry) updated; workstream 004 gains s05 delivering req-09 with a changelog row. Mutation receipts for each guard in assets/proof.md. The PR's `Delivers:` line names workstream 004 s05 and req-09.

Notices name a count, not seats (F205, req-09; F192-style noise). Every notice `transition()` builds gives the number of live proxied seats and where to list them, `Proxied seats: 43 (`just doctor` lists them)`, never the seat ids (cap 0). `pij-rs cache-proxy status` talks only to the sidecar and lists no seats, so the notice names `just doctor` (its `cache seats:` line) and `/health.cache_proxy.seats`. Notice tests assert the count and that no seat id appears.

value.title: Sidecar status off the upstream path, stale-answer rule, watch debounce, gate retry
value.brief: All nine ACs, one lane (coder/230, pij-fair-firefly), one PR. Sidecar half (crates/cache-proxy) first, then the daemon half (crates/daemon/src/cache_proxy.rs), then live proof on a private daemon and a sidecar on a test port with a stalling fake upstream.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: Code map (origin/main 81b459c4). Sidecar: `Proxy::status()` (crates/cache-proxy/src/proxy.rs) awaits `run_check(false)`, which takes `check_lock` and, when `checked_at` is older than CHECK_TTL (600 s) or FAILED_CHECK_TTL (60 s) or `recheck` is set, runs `readiness::check` (two GETs, 15 s timeout each). `reload()` runs `run_check(true)` then returns `status()`. The router holds `Arc<Proxy>`, so the status handler can spawn the background check. `forward()` reads `(generation, bearer)` per attempt but calls `quota_refused()`/`quota_served()` with no account or generation. Daemon: `CacheProxy::read()` (crates/daemon/src/cache_proxy.rs) maps a timeout and any other send error to `Reading::Unreachable`; `observe()` stores `reading.state()` and `transition()` notices on any change; `gate()` reads once. `/health.cache_proxy` is `HealthView`; `just doctor`'s `cache seats:` line reads it from `pij-rs --json ping`. Findings covered: F204 (pm-001 LOG 2026-11-18: one slow probe made a false outage notice naming 43 seats); the stale 402 (takin's s04 row 12 finding, 2026-11-18 15:00: a 402 on a request sent before an account switch latched `quota_exhausted` on the new account until a reload); F205 (prime far-jackal: every notice lists every proxied seat to every prime).

value.risk: A status read during the first stale window serves the old state for up to one check round trip.
value.mitigation: By design (packet): the cached state is the last known truth; `checked_at_ms` lets a reader see its age; state changes still settle when the check lands.

value.risk: A background check races a reload or refresh.
value.mitigation: It takes the same `check_lock` and keeps the generation check that drops facts read with a replaced token; F001 and F002 regressions stay green.

value.risk: A real hang is reported 30 s later than today.
value.mitigation: A refusal (the common death) is still told at once; a hang is told on the 2nd read, 30 s later, which the packet accepts.

value.risk: The gate retry holds the spawn lock for up to 2 s on a hung sidecar.
value.mitigation: Only after a timeout, still bounded; with the status route off the upstream path a timeout means a hung sidecar.

Proof on a private daemon (own state dir and socket) and a sidecar on a test port with a fake upstream; never the prod daemon, port 7471 or the LaunchAgent (s04's live window is on them).
Never read credential files or print a token; never type into a pane this seat did not create.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`, no `npm install`; trailers Pij-Seat: pij-fair-firefly, Pij-Prime: pij-far-jackal, Pij-Plan: 230-cache-proxy-watch, plus Co-Authored-By.
